title: Haivision Unveils Makito ONE Live Video Contribution Platform
body_html:
What Was Announced

Haivision has introduced the Makito ONE live video contribution platform, a solution aimed at enhancing the efficiency and reliability of live video contribution workflows. This platform is designed to address the complexities of live video transmission, providing a robust and scalable solution for broadcasters and media organizations. By leveraging advanced technologies, the Makito ONE platform seeks to simplify the process of acquiring and distributing live video content, thereby reducing operational overhead and improving overall workflow efficiency.

The Engineering and Operational Significance

The Makito ONE platform holds significant technical importance as it has the potential to streamline live video contribution workflows by providing a more reliable, scalable, and flexible solution. From an engineering perspective, this platform can help mitigate issues related to signal latency, packet loss, and video quality degradation, which are common challenges in live video transmission. By utilizing advanced compression algorithms and transport protocols, the Makito ONE platform can ensure high-quality video transmission over IP networks, making it an attractive solution for broadcasters seeking to migrate from traditional SDI-based infrastructures to more agile and flexible IP-based architectures. Furthermore, the platform's ability to support multiple video formats and protocols, including SMPTE ST 2110, AES67, and SRT, enables seamless integration with existing broadcast ecosystems, including MAM, playout, and graphics systems.

Industry Context

The introduction of the Makito ONE platform comes at a time when the broadcast industry is undergoing a significant transformation, driven by the adoption of IP-based technologies, cloud-based services, and software-defined architectures. As broadcasters seek to improve their operational efficiency, reduce costs, and enhance their ability to deliver high-quality content to multiple platforms, solutions like the Makito ONE platform are gaining traction. The platform's focus on live video contribution aligns with the industry's shift towards more agile and flexible production workflows, which are capable of supporting a wide range of formats, including 4K, HDR, and immersive audio. Moreover, the Makito ONE platform competes with other live video contribution solutions, such as those offered by vendors like Net Insight, Nevion, and VideoFlow, which are also vying for market share in this rapidly evolving space.

Implications for Broadcast and Media Teams

The introduction of the Makito ONE platform has significant implications for broadcast and media teams, particularly those responsible for live production, ingest, and playout operations. Engineering teams should carefully evaluate the platform's technical capabilities, assessing its ability to integrate with existing workflows, including MAM, PAM, and automation systems. Operations managers should consider the potential benefits of the Makito ONE platform in terms of reduced operational overhead, improved video quality, and enhanced reliability, as well as its ability to support multi-platform delivery, including OTT, social media, and CDN-based distribution. Moreover, platform teams should investigate the platform's support for emerging technologies, such as 5G, edge computing, and artificial intelligence, which are poised to play a critical role in the future of live video production and distribution. By doing so, broadcast and media teams can determine whether the Makito ONE platform aligns with their strategic objectives and can help them achieve their goals of improving efficiency, flexibility, and resilience in their live video workflows.
